emptyDirs.emptyFolder.reason: Contains no files at all. Placeholder folders that programs create by convention are excluded.
emptyDirs.brokenShortcut.label: Dead shortcut
emptyDirs.brokenShortcut.reason: Its target no longer exists — clicking it only produces an error dialog.
emptyDirs.zeroByte.label: Zero-byte file
emptyDirs.zeroByte.reason: The file exists but has no contents — usually left by an interrupted download or write.
emptyDirs.noRoot: None of Desktop, Documents or Downloads could be resolved
software.rarelyUsedHint: Over 500 MB and untouched for more than 90 days. This is the group worth looking at first.
execute.browserRunning: Nothing could be deleted — the browser is most likely still running. Close it completely and try again.
tuning.title: Tuning
tuning.description: The preset decides which categories run; these decide what counts as junk. Changes apply on the next scan.
toolbox.searchPlaceholder: Type a tool name or the problem it solves…
toolbox.badHost: That host name contains characters that are not allowed
toolbox.badPort: The port must be between 1 and 65535
toolbox.fileTooLarge: That file is too large for this tool
toolbox.shredderSsdNote: On an SSD, overwriting does not guarantee the original data is gone: wear levelling writes the new bytes to a different physical block. Full-disk encryption is what actually works.
toolbox.processList.label: Process memory ranking
toolbox.processList.description: Processes sorted by memory, with the publisher. Task Manager needs a right-click into Properties to show who owns each one.
toolbox.serviceList.label: Non-Microsoft services
toolbox.serviceList.description: Only services installed by third-party software. Read-only: stopping the wrong one costs far more than it saves.
toolbox.diskHealth.label: Disk health
toolbox.diskHealth.description: Health status, power-on hours and wear per physical disk. Values that cannot be read are left blank rather than invented.
toolbox.restorePointList.label: Restore points
toolbox.restorePointList.description: The restore points that already exist. Windows buries this list four dialogs deep.
toolbox.pendingReboot.label: Pending reboot check
toolbox.pendingReboot.description: Whether updates are waiting for a reboot. A lot of "I cleaned but nothing changed" turns out to be this.
toolbox.bigFileFinder.label: Find large files
toolbox.bigFileFinder.description: Finds the largest files under a folder you pick. No cleaning capability at all — it only shows you.
toolbox.fileHash.label: File checksum
toolbox.fileHash.description: Computes SHA-256 and MD5 for a file so you can check it against the value published by the vendor.
toolbox.bulkAttributes.label: Clear read-only & hidden
toolbox.bulkAttributes.description: Clears read-only and hidden across a whole folder tree. Preview by default; it only writes when you tick Apply.
toolbox.brokenShortcutScan.label: Scan for dead shortcuts
toolbox.brokenShortcutScan.description: Finds .lnk files pointing at targets that no longer exist. Listing only — deletion lives in the Empty folders category.
toolbox.recycleBinStatus.label: Recycle Bin usage
toolbox.recycleBinStatus.description: How much is in the Recycle Bin and how big it is. Uses the shell API, which is more accurate than walking the folder.
toolbox.fileShredder.label: Shred a file
toolbox.fileShredder.description: Three overwrite passes, then rename and delete. It does not promise irrecoverability on SSDs, and says so before you run it.
toolbox.clearRecentDocs.label: Clear recent files
toolbox.clearRecentDocs.description: Wipes Explorer's recent list and jump lists in one go. The thing you press before handing your laptop to someone.
toolbox.pingTest.label: Latency test
toolbox.pingTest.description: Latency and packet loss to a host. Defaults to an address reachable from mainland China so a blocked target is not misreported as "no network".
toolbox.dnsServers.label: DNS servers
toolbox.dnsServers.description: Which DNS each adapter is actually using. First thing to check when pages will not load.
toolbox.killPort.label: Free a busy port
toolbox.killPort.description: Finds what is holding a port and, after you confirm, ends it. Look-only by default.
junk.pipCache.label: pip package cache
junk.pipCache.reason: Wheel cache left behind when installing Python packages. Removing it only means the next install re-downloads; your environment is untouched.
junk.npmCache.label: npm package cache
junk.npmCache.reason: Tarballs npm has downloaded. Removing it only means the next install re-fetches; node_modules is untouched.
junk.yarnCache.label: Yarn package cache
junk.yarnCache.reason: Packages Yarn has downloaded. Removing it means the next install re-fetches them.
junk.goBuildCache.label: Go build cache
junk.goBuildCache.reason: Intermediate Go compilation output. Removing it only makes the next build slower - no network needed.
junk.vscodeCache.label: VS Code cache
junk.vscodeCache.reason: The editor's network and workspace cache; rebuilt automatically on next launch.
junk.vscodeCachedData.label: VS Code precompiled data
junk.vscodeCachedData.reason: V8 precompiled code left over from older versions, largely unused after an upgrade.
junk.gradleCache.label: Gradle dependency cache
junk.gradleCache.reason: Every dependency your Android/Java builds downloaded. Removing it means the next build re-downloads several GB - think twice on a metered connection.
junk.goModCache.label: Go module cache
junk.goModCache.reason: Go module sources already downloaded. Removing it means the next build re-downloads them.
junk.cargoRegistry.label: Cargo dependency cache
junk.cargoRegistry.reason: Crates Rust has downloaded. Removing it means the next build re-downloads them.
junk.nugetPackages.label: NuGet package cache
junk.nugetPackages.reason: Packages .NET has downloaded. Removing it means the next restore re-downloads them.
junk.electronCache.label: Electron download cache
junk.electronCache.reason: Electron binaries per version, roughly 100-200 MB each. Removing it means the next build re-downloads them.
junk.playwrightBrowsers.label: Playwright browsers
junk.playwrightBrowsers.reason: Browser engines used for automated tests. Removing them means running `playwright install` again (hundreds of MB).
junk.jetbrainsCaches.label: JetBrains caches and indexes
junk.jetbrainsCaches.reason: IDE indexes and logs. Removing them means reindexing the next time you open a project - minutes on a large one.
junk.androidAvd.label: Android emulator images
junk.androidAvd.reason: These are virtual devices you created, not a cache - so this row only shows how much space they take and offers no delete. Remove them from Android Studio's Device Manager, where you can actually tell the emulators apart.
health.needsSeparateAnalysis: Size not measured yet - this entry needs a separate analysis (about {{minutes}} min), run it from the Disk space tab. No number here does not mean there is nothing to reclaim.
junk.devCachesPending.label: Developer tool caches (not scanned)
junk.devCachesPending.reason: gradle / go / cargo / NuGet / Electron / Playwright / JetBrains caches and Android emulator images. These directories routinely hold hundreds of thousands of files and take tens of seconds to walk, which would make the one-click checkup a button nobody dares press - so they are skipped by default. Scan them from the Disk space tab.
history.title: Cleanup history
history.lastDeltaHint: Free space on the system drive, measured before and after. It will not match "freed in total" - that figure sums the size of each entry, while hard links, files held open, and items merely moved to the Recycle Bin never turn into real free space.
startup.delayFailed: Could not set up the delayed start
startup.delayUnsupported: This entry cannot be delayed (only registry Run entries can)
startup.delayCreateFailed: Could not create the scheduled task
browser.runningWarning: This browser is running, so it holds its cache files open and part of the cleanup will fail. Close it first if you want the freed space to match the figure shown.
impactHint.cache: Rebuilt automatically. You will not notice any difference.
impactHint.history: Clears 'recently opened' and browsing history. Nothing stops working.
impactHint.signin: Sites will sign you out and you will have to log in again.
impactHint.config: Settings you configured by hand go back to their defaults.
impactHint.userdata: Your own files or data. Recovering means going to a backup.
impactHint.system: A system component or driver. Recovery may mean reinstalling.
cleanLevel.label: Cleanup level
cleanLevel.conservativeHint: Only items that cost nothing to rebuild
cleanLevel.standardHint: Suggested items, skipping the costly ones
safety.protected.quickAccessPinned: This file holds the folders you pinned to Quick access in File Explorer. It looks like a usage trace but it is your own setting, and Windows does not rebuild it — so this item is never cleaned.
safety.protected.installedWebApp: This is where the browser keeps your installed web apps (PWAs). Deleting it leaves them broken or iconless, so this item is never cleaned.
safety.demoted.irreversible: This cannot be undone and is expensive to rebuild, so it is not ticked for you. Tick it yourself if you want it gone.
privacy.protectedHint: {{count}} of these are items you pinned yourself. They are excluded and will not be cleaned.
browser.closeFirst: In use by {{process}} — close it before cleaning.
execute.closeFirst: Skipped: another program is holding this open. Close it and try again.
confirm.blockedLine: {{count}} items are held open by another program and will be skipped. Closing that program first gets everything in one pass.
columns.title: Columns
riskLevelHint.low: The worst this costs you is half a second the next time something loads. The system rebuilds it on its own, so this tier is safe to tick without reading it.
riskLevelHint.medium: You will notice this one: a site may ask you to sign in again, or a setting may fall back to its default. Recoverable, but it costs you minutes.
riskLevelHint.high: This can leave a program unable to start, or a record gone for good. Read what it is before you tick it, and do not tick it just because it is large.
privacy.jumpListsCustom.label: Taskbar jump lists (custom entries)
privacy.jumpListsCustom.reason: The jump-list entries you pinned yourself in a taskbar right-click menu, plus the custom lists that apps register for themselves. Clearing them makes them vanish from the menu immediately, and they do not come back on their own: an app can only re-register its list the next time it runs, and most apps never do — for those it is gone for good. That is why this one is off by default.
toolbox.protectedSkipped_one: Kept {{count}} item: it is protected content and was not deleted.
toolbox.protectedSkipped_other: Kept {{count}} items: they are protected content and were not deleted.
toolbox.recentDocsPinnedNote: This clears recent-usage traces only. Anything you pinned to Quick access or to a taskbar jump list is left untouched, and you will be told how many were kept.
